issues.sym: A clicking or clunking from a wheel, a vibration that gets worse, or in the worst case a wheel coming off.
issues.why: The hub bolts on early cars could loosen after only a few hundred miles from sharp turns and hard braking.
issues.next: Check your VIN for both hub bolt recalls. The dealer fixes the hubs for free. Stop driving right away if you hear clunking from a wheel.

issues.t: Defroster and heat stop working from A/C compressor fault (recall)
issues.sym: The heater blows cold, the windshield won't defrost or defog, and warning messages may appear. Some owners report the A/C quitting in hot weather too.
issues.why: A fault in the electric A/C compressor or its controls can shut down the whole climate system. Because this car uses the compressor as a heat pump, losing it means losing heat and defrost too. Owners report long waits for parts.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. The dealer updates the climate software and replaces the compressor if needed, for free. Don't drive if you can't clear the windshield.

issues.t: Rearview camera freezes or goes blank (recall)
issues.sym: When you shift into Reverse, the camera picture freezes or the screen stays blank.
issues.why: A software error in the parking-assist system on cars with the surround-view camera can stop the backup image from showing.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. The dealer updates the software for free. Look behind you and use the mirrors until it is fixed.

issues.t: Loss of drive power from a battery control fault (recall)
issues.sym: Warning messages on the dash and a sudden loss of power while driving.
issues.why: The control unit that manages the high-voltage battery can develop a software fault and cut drive power.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. The dealer updates the battery control software for free. If power drops, steer to a safe spot and stop.

issues.t: 12-volt battery goes dead, car won't start or unlock
issues.sym: The car won't power on or unlock, often after sitting, or the battery dies more than once. Cold weather makes it worse.
issues.why: Owners report the small 12-volt battery running flat even though the big drive battery is charged. The 12-volt battery runs the computers that start the car.
issues.next: Keep a jump pack handy. Have the dealer test the 12-volt battery and check for software updates that change how it is charged.

issues.t: Sudden power loss or EV system malfunction warning
issues.sym: Messages like "EV System Malfunction" appear, and the car may lose power on the highway, especially in cold weather.
issues.why: Owners report drive system faults that leave them stranded. Causes vary and some were tied to battery or climate system faults.
issues.next: Get to a safe spot and stop. Have the car towed to a dealer and ask them to check for the related recalls and software updates.

issues.t: Wheel-well liners or underbody covers torn loose
issues.sym: Scraping or flapping noises after driving through deep water or heavy rain, or plastic panels hanging under the car.
issues.why: Owners report the wheel-well liners and underbody covers tearing off in standing water, in one case exposing high-voltage cables. Some dealers denied warranty coverage.
issues.next: Avoid deep standing water. Have loose panels reattached right away and ask the dealer to check the high-voltage wiring.

issues.t: Slow DC fast charging, especially in cold weather
issues.sym: DC fast charging tops out at a low rate, far below what the car is rated for, and takes much longer in the cold.
issues.why: The battery protects itself by limiting charge speed when cold. Owners also report charging stuck at low rates with no fault found.
issues.next: Precondition by driving before fast charging in cold weather, and try a different charger. Ask the dealer for charging software updates.

issues.t: Real-world range far below the estimate
issues.sym: You get noticeably fewer miles per charge than the rating, and the range shown drops quickly in winter.
issues.why: Cold weather, heater use and highway speed all cut range. Owners report big gaps between the estimate and real use.
issues.next: Use seat heaters instead of cabin heat when you can, and precondition while plugged in. Have the battery checked if range drops suddenly.

issues.t: Car lurches or speeds up while parking
issues.sym: The car moves forward or backward unexpectedly while parking, sometimes hitting something.
issues.why: Several owners report this to NHTSA. Some suspect a regenerative braking or software fault. Dealers often report finding no defect.
issues.next: Report it to Subaru and NHTSA and ask the dealer to save the event data. Park slowly with your foot covering the brake.

issues.t: Regenerative braking cuts in or out unexpectedly
issues.sym: Slowing down feels different from one moment to the next, or the car stops more sharply than you expect on slippery roads.
issues.why: Owners report regenerative braking switching off at random, which needs more brake pedal, or grabbing on snow.
issues.next: Be ready to use the brake pedal and leave extra room in snow. Have the dealer check for software updates.

issues.t: Adaptive cruise doesn't detect cars ahead in rain
issues.sym: In rain or mist, adaptive cruise control fails to slow for a car in front of you.
issues.why: The front radar and camera can lose sight of other cars in bad weather. Owners report it happening more than once.
issues.next: Don't rely on adaptive cruise in rain or fog. Keep the front sensors clean and ask the dealer about software updates.

issues.t: Driver monitor and lane assist false alerts
issues.sym: The driver camera says it can't see you, the car brakes with nothing ahead, or lane-keeping steers more than expected.
issues.why: Owners report the driver monitoring camera and lane-keeping systems acting up.
issues.next: Keep the driver camera lens clean. Turn lane assist off if it pulls oddly and have the dealer check the system.

issues.t: Bluetooth or app features keep dropping
issues.sym: Your phone disconnects during calls or navigation, or remote features in the app don't work.
issues.why: Owners report connection and app problems that dealers could not fix.
issues.next: Delete and re-pair your phone, update the phone and car software, and report it to the dealer.

issues.t: Clicking from the front suspension over bumps
issues.sym: A click from the front left when going over speed bumps at low speed.
issues.why: An owner reports the noise, and the dealer could not reproduce it.
issues.next: Note when it happens and have the front suspension inspected.

issues.sym: Things look wavy or warped through the windshield, which can be tiring or make you feel queasy.
issues.why: An owner reports optical distortion in the windshield glass.
issues.next: Have the dealer look at the glass. A replacement may be covered under warranty.

issues.t: Headlights flicker or shake over bumps
issues.sym: At night the low beams seem to flicker, strobe or jump on bumpy roads.
issues.why: Several owners of 2026 cars report it. Some think the headlight mounting moves and the sharp LED beam edge makes small movements look like flicker.
issues.next: Note the conditions and show the dealer. Ask them to check the headlight mounts and aim.

issues.t: Automatic braking or lane assist acts on its own
issues.sym: The brakes apply with nothing ahead, or lane-keeping jerks the wheel. One owner hit a curb.
issues.why: Owners of 2026 cars report the driver-assist sensors reacting to things that are not there. One dealer blamed wheel alignment.
issues.next: Report each event to the dealer and NHTSA. Have the alignment and the front camera and radar calibration checked.
